current_row.boundary_rationale: The narration turns to Jeremiah’s own first-person voice, וַיֹּ֖אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֑הוּ הָיָ֥ה דְּבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.32.6, byte tier), matching “Jeremiah said, Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,” (web:Jer.32.6) — the command phase of the sign that follows opens at once with a named relative arriving, “Behold, Hanamel the son of Shallum your uncle will come to you, saying,” (web:Jer.32.7), sent to buy “my field that is in Anathoth” (web:Jer.32.7). The performance follows without any further command, וַיָּבֹ֣א אֵ֠לַי חֲנַמְאֵ֨ל בֶּן דֹּדִ֜י כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָה֮ אֶל חֲצַ֣ר הַמַּטָּרָה֒ (oshb:Jer.32.8, byte), matching “So Hanamel my uncle’s son came to me in the court of the guard according to Yahweh’s word” (web:Jer.32.8) — a WEB paragraph break falls inside this very verse, between the arrival and Jeremiah’s own closing note that he then knew the word was Yahweh’s, a modern formatting fold rather than any textual seam. The purchase itself, the weighing of silver, the sealing and witnessing of the deed, and its delivery to Baruch all continue this same first-person report through וָֽאֲצַוֶּה֙ אֶת בָּר֔וּךְ לְעֵינֵיהֶ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר (oshb:Jer.32.13, byte), matching “I commanded Baruch before them, saying,” (web:Jer.32.13), which opens the interpretation phase: כֹּֽה אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Jer.32.14, byte), matching “Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel, says:” (web:Jer.32.14), charging that the deeds be preserved “that they may last many days” (web:Jer.32.14), and closing on the reason given for the whole sign, כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָא֖וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל (oshb:Jer.32.15, byte), matching “For Yahweh of Armies, the God of Israel says: ‘Houses and fields and vineyards will yet again be bought in this land.’” (web:Jer.32.15). Command, performance, and interpretation are held here as one unit because no addressee shift, frame-owner change, or discourse imperative interrupts them anywhere in between; the seam comes only where Jeremiah turns from reporting the purchase to reporting his own prayer, “I prayed to Yahweh, saying,” (web:Jer.32.16), and this row is bounded there.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A prayer-frame verb opens the unit on its own, וָאֶתְפַּלֵּ֖ל אֶל יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.32.16, byte), matching “I prayed to Yahweh, saying,” (web:Jer.32.16), turning Jeremiah’s own report from narrating the purchase to addressing God directly. The address opens with a vocative divine title, אֲהָהּ֮ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִה֒ (oshb:Jer.32.17, byte), matching “Ah Lord Yahweh! Behold, you have made the heavens and the earth by your great power” (web:Jer.32.17), and states as its own premise “There is nothing too hard for you” (web:Jer.32.17). Praise of Yahweh’s power and justice continues through a recital of the exodus, the gift of the land, and Israel’s own disobedience, unbroken by any new addressee, until a fresh “Behold” turns the address to the present siege, הִנֵּ֣ה הַסֹּלְל֗וֹת בָּ֣אוּ הָעִיר֮ (oshb:Jer.32.24, byte), matching “Behold, siege ramps have been built against the city to take it” (web:Jer.32.24). It closes on the tension between the command just carried out and the circumstance surrounding it, וְאַתָּ֞ה אָמַ֤רְתָּ אֵלַי֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה (oshb:Jer.32.25, byte), matching “You have said to me, Lord Yahweh, ‘Buy the field for money, and call witnesses;’” (web:Jer.32.25), “whereas the city is given into the hand of the Chaldeans” (web:Jer.32.25). This whole address to God is held as one unit because it is never interrupted by a new addressee or a change of speaker — it moves from praise through historical recital to present crisis and an unresolved question without ever leaving Jeremiah’s own voice directed at Yahweh; the next word-event formula reopens address as Yahweh’s own reply, “Then Yahweh’s word came to Jeremiah, saying,” (web:Jer.32.26), and this row ends just short of it.
current_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Typing this span as a hymn of praise rather than a lament was considered, since verses 17 through 23 are sustained creation-and-exodus praise close in shape to the doxologies elsewhere in the book; it is held here as a personal address to God running to an unresolved question instead, since the unit does not close on praise but on Jeremiah’s own bewildered complaint at the gap between command and circumstance, the same shape the book’s confessions take even though this address carries none of their persecution content.
current_row.literature_type_guess: Jeremiah’s own prayer over the field he has just bought

The bytes separate the two objects at these sites too: the full stack stands in 32 verses (Jer.25.27 inside P09-003's span; Jer.32.14 and Jer.32.15 inside P12-002's), whereas the formulas the three blended rows actually splice carry NO tsevaot -- וְעַתָּ֕ה לָכֵ֛ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י (oshb:Jer.32.36, byte tier) and כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל (oshb:Jer.34.2, byte tier) -- so the blended key also mis-files them under the full-stack object.
findings.proposed_cure: Rewrite the five entries to the settled split -- divine_title.yhwh_tsevaot_elohei_yisrael + speech_formula.koh_amar_yhwh for P09-003 and P12-002, and speech_formula.koh_amar_yhwh with a tsevaot-free divine_title key for P12-005, P13-001 and P13-003.

findings.byte_evidence: 'byte' is collate.py's Hebrew quote-collation tier (byte / nfd / accent_stripped / skeleton / none) and asserts that a quoted run matches the source bytes; these citations quote nothing. The parashah and paseq layers are explicitly not verse bytes -- pmarks_Jer.json paseq_note: seg layer, NOT quotable verse bytes, citable from this inventory only -- so a byte label on them claims a tier the seg layer cannot carry. 17 occurrences across these 6 rows; the same rows label their real Hebrew splices correctly and no other row in this scope does it. check_marks.py is GREEN over these 48 rows (flag_count 0): it validates the seg TYPE and the MT key, not the tier word.
findings.proposed_cure: Drop the tier word from every seg-layer citation, leaving the plain MT key plus the single-witness disclosure already present.
